---
title: "Foundations"
---


The numbers this universe runs on, and the constraints it may not break.

This entry is the root of the encyclopedia. Everything else derives from it, and
nothing in it derives from anything else. Its companion is
guide-master-plan, which holds the *why*; this file holds the *how much* and
the *what may not happen*.

## How to use this file

**Constants are cited, never restated.** Every number in the Transcendent
Chronicles lives in exactly one place — the table below — and every other entry
refers to it by ID. An entry that writes out a figure instead of citing it will
drift the first time the figure changes, and the figures have changed once
already.

**Invariants are falsifiable.** They are not themes or preferences. Each one can
be checked against a claim and can be shown to be violated. An entry that
contradicts an invariant is wrong, not interesting.

Entries declare what they rest on in their frontmatter:

```yaml
derives_from: [I-04, C-01, propulsion]
```

`bin/tc-check` validates that every cited ID exists, that the derivation graph
has no cycles, that no entry restates a guarded value without citing its
constant, and that every named world orbits a star in
`lore/data/nearby-stars.csv`. The star catalog is the one place where this
encyclopedia is checkable against something outside itself: the F/G/K rows and
their habitability judgements come from Sol Company's ten-parsec tables, and the
M-dwarf rows from a SIMBAD query for everything with a parallax above 100
milliarcseconds — which is exactly the ten-parsec boundary.

The **Guard** column names a literal string the checker watches for. If an entry
contains that string without citing the constant that owns it, the check fails.
Constants whose values appear too often in ordinary prose are left unguarded
rather than made noisy: `30 ly` and `0.2c` are ordinary measurements, and
`C-07`'s bare `~150` and `C-10`'s bare `~250` collide with durations —
the Expansion wave takes ~150 years and the Synthetic Wars run ~250. Where a
figure is guardable but its digits are not distinctive, the guard carries a
word of context — `~80 locked` rather than `~80`. A guard that fires on
innocent prose is worse than no guard, because a noisy gate is one people
learn to route around.

## Invariants

| ID | Invariant |
|---|---|
| `I-01` | No FTL travel exists except the [thorne-nexus](/encyclopedia/thorne-nexus.html). Warp is subluminal, always |
| `I-02` | No gate mouth may be transported by a method carrying relativistic gamma |
| `I-03` | The Nexus contains no cycles |
| `I-04` | No Genesis seedship carried adult humans or any human crew |
| `I-05` | Nothing with local velocity exceeds `C-17` through unswept space |
| `I-06` | Alcubierre vessels have no local velocity, no time dilation, and no momentum |
| `I-07` | No colony invented a technology. Every drive's theory arrived complete in the Guide corpus |
| `I-08` | No non-human sapients exist **within the diaspora's reach**. Every intelligence in recorded history descends from Earth, was built by something that did, or is a Guide. Whether the wider galaxy is inhabited is unknown and must stay unknown |
| `I-09` | Every named star exists in the real 10 pc catalog, at its real distance and spectral class |
| `I-10` | No Genesis colony lies beyond `C-01` from Sol |
| `I-11` | A sleeping Guide answers; it does not act. Oracle invocation only |
| `I-12` | AI technology was withheld from every colony |
| `I-14` | Habitability has two axes: irradiance tier 0–7 and rotational state free/locked |
| `I-15` | Vault release thresholds are mechanical and gameable. No Guide judges them after sleep |

## On the emptiness of the neighbourhood

`I-08` says the diaspora met nobody. It does not say the galaxy is empty, and no
entry may treat the one as evidence for the other.

Orion's reach is `C-01` — a bubble of `C-06` good systems inside a galaxy of
`C-21` stars. At its height the Confederacy held some two thousand systems,
roughly one part in a hundred million of the whole. Finding nobody in a sample
that size is not evidence of absence. It is not evidence of anything.

The galaxy may be crowded. The only others humanity ever found were itself.

Dates and eras live in [galactic-timeline](/encyclopedia/galactic-timeline.html). The calendar systems live in
[stellar-calendar](/encyclopedia/stellar-calendar.html). The star catalog is `lore/data/nearby-stars.csv`, which is
data rather than prose and is not an encyclopedia entry.
